messages.subject: Help to understand results
parts:
Warm greetings,

I hope you are doing well. My name is Santiago Hernández, I'm a biology student in La Universidad de La Salle de Colombia.
I contacted Eric last year for advice and help interpreting some Distance data. I see that he is no longer at St Andrews, so I am reaching out to you; I really hope you can help, as I haven't been able to make much progress on my thesis project due to not fully understanding the results.

I’ve had to pause my project on the population density of *Cistothorus apolinari*; there have been some fires here in Colombia that required attention, and work commitments also forced me to postpone the research. However, I have now decided to resume the project, with the aim of providing tools for the conservation of this bird and the Andean *páramos*.

I shared the data in zip file. I would appreciate it if you could review them and share your thoughts. Based on the AIC values and the number of parameters, I identified analysis number 10 as the best model. However, I have a few questions regarding the "Expected cluster size" and "Density & abundance" windows. Is the average cluster size calculated per count point or for the entire sampled area? The same applies to the population density estimates: do the populations in the Laguna de Socha and Peña Negra sectors consist of 23 and 36 individuals, respectively? Does *Distance* provide a final density estimate for just a single sampling point or for the entire sampled area? Does the final value we see represent the total number of individuals in the entire area?

Thank you in advance for your patience and for taking the time to read this. It would be a great help if you were willing to collaborate, though I also understand that you have other responsibilities, so I completely understand if you are unable to reply.

Thanks again, and I hope we stay in touch. Best regards from Colombia.
P.S.: I look forward to the next Distance course so I can participate.
